REQ releases contain forecast and historical workbooks plus a report PDF.
`read_req_forecasts()` parses 21 data sheets and classifies two metadata
sheets. `read_req_history()` parses Tables 1–41 across 44 data sheets and
classifies three metadata sheets. Tables 2, 7 and 24 have separate `(1)` and
`(2)` source labels; those labels remain provenance while each part gets a
stable semantic `table_id`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
reported <- read_req("req-2026-06", view = "reported")
table(reported$source_dataset, reported$source_sheet)
```

Workbook order is not meaningful. Sheet selection uses normalized titles and
structural fingerprints: header labels, period patterns, section labels and
unit placement. Unknown structures raise `req_workbook_schema_error`.

Every row retains the exact release, source workbook, source sheet, content
hash and parser version. The report PDF is cached for narrative and validation;
it is not used for OCR table extraction.
